paragraphs.title: Jerusalem’s Holiness and God’s Love for Zion

easy.explanation: Verse 1 says, “His foundation is in the holy mountains.”
easy.q: Where is the foundation of the city described in the psalm?

answers: All the dwellings of Jacob only
easy.explanation: Verse 2 says, “The LORD loveth the gates of Zion.”
Verse 3 calls Jerusalem “the city of God.”
easy.q: How is Jerusalem described in verse 3?

answers: The LORD loves Zion’s gates more than all Jacob’s dwellings
The LORD does not love Jacob’s dwellings
Zion and Jacob’s dwellings are unrelated
medium.explanation: The verse says the LORD loves Zion’s gates “more than all the dwellings of Jacob.”
medium.q: What comparison is made between Zion’s gates and Jacob’s dwellings?

medium.explanation: “Glorious things” refers to honorable and excellent things spoken about the city.
medium.q: What does “glorious things” mean in verse 3?

answers: The mountains are mentioned as another unrelated place
Jerusalem’s foundation is in the holy mountains
medium.explanation: Verse 1 presents the city as founded in the holy mountains.
medium.q: What connection does the psalm make between the holy mountains and Jerusalem?

answers: Jerusalem has a central and special place in the psalm
The psalm concerns only Jacob’s dwellings
challenge.explanation: These descriptions emphasize Jerusalem’s unique importance.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the LORD’s love for Zion’s gates and the glorious things spoken about it?

challenge.explanation: The expression “the city of God” directly links Jerusalem with God.
challenge.q: Which expression most directly connects Jerusalem with God?

answers: They describe it as a place of war
They compare it with every country
They mention its holiness, God’s love, and its glory
challenge.explanation: The verses mention the holy mountains, the LORD’s love, and glorious things spoken about the city.
challenge.q: Why do the first three verses present Jerusalem with great honor?

paragraphs.title: Zion as the Birthplace of Many Distinguished People

answers: Rahab, Babylon, Philistia, Tyre, and Ethiopia
easy.explanation: Verse 4 names Rahab, Babylon, Philistia, Tyre, and Ethiopia.
easy.q: Which places are named among the nations mentioned in the psalm?

answers: This and that man was born in her
It was built upon the sea
easy.explanation: Verse 5 says, “This and that man was born in her.”
easy.q: What shall be said of Zion?

easy.explanation: Verse 6 says, “The LORD shall count, when he writeth up the people.”
easy.q: Who shall count the people when they are written up?

answers: It compares Zion with the countries of the world
It describes a journey by the children of Israel
It lists only the cities of Zion
medium.explanation: The verse names various places and sets them alongside Zion.
medium.q: What does verse 4 accomplish by mentioning several lands and peoples?

medium.explanation: The phrase refers to a person’s place of birth.
medium.q: What does the phrase “was born there” mean in this passage?

answers: The LORD will prevent Zion from existing
The verse makes no connection between them
medium.explanation: After speaking of Zion, the verse says that the highest himself shall establish her.
medium.q: What connection is made between the LORD and Zion in verse 5?

answers: Zion is presented as especially important to Him
The LORD does not know who was born there
Zion is presented as having no inhabitants
challenge.explanation: The LORD’s counting and recording show recognition and importance.
challenge.q: What may be signified by the LORD recognizing those recorded as born in Zion?

answers: A description of the city gates only
Zion as a place connected with birth and the recognition of many people
A description of springs and dancing
challenge.explanation: These verses focus on people being associated with Zion through birth and divine recognition.
challenge.q: What common idea links verses 4 through 6?

answers: Birth in Zion is a central idea in the passage
The psalm describes only a geographical location
Birth has no connection with Zion
challenge.explanation: The repeated reference to birth highlights Zion as a special birthplace.
challenge.q: What does the repeated idea of being born in Zion emphasize?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “As well the singers as the players on instruments shall be there.”
easy.q: Who is mentioned as being present in verse 7?

answers: In the countries of the world
easy.explanation: The verse ends with the words, “all my springs are in thee.”
easy.q: Where are all the springs according to the verse?

easy.explanation: Their singing and playing express joyful praise directed toward Zion.
easy.q: What do the singers and players do?

medium.explanation: The springs can represent the hopes and longings that flow toward Zion.
medium.q: What can the “springs” symbolize in the idea of this passage?

answers: They express joy and praise directed toward it
They have no connection with it
medium.explanation: The musicians’ presence conveys joyful praise associated with Zion.
medium.q: How are singing and playing related to Jerusalem?

answers: All hopes and longings are directed toward Jerusalem
All springs are located outside Jerusalem
Only the singers are connected with Jerusalem
medium.explanation: The expression portrays Zion as the source and focus of every hope and longing.
medium.q: What does “all my springs are in thee” mean in the context of the psalm?

answers: The connection with Zion is lively, joyful, and full of longing
The connection with Zion is distant and cold
challenge.explanation: Music expresses joy, while springs suggest flowing hopes and desires.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the combination of singing, playing, and springs?

challenge.explanation: The word “all” gives the statement its complete and inclusive meaning.
challenge.q: Which word emphasizes that the longing is not limited to one thing?

answers: It adds the joyful praise and longing of singers and musicians for Zion
It repeats only the names of foreign countries
challenge.explanation: After describing Zion’s holiness and importance, the verse presents joyful praise and longing directed toward it.
challenge.q: How does verse 7 complete the ideas in the earlier verses?
